policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV "Now Peter and John were going up into the temple" has no rendering of ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ("together", as KJV prints it); the bare Πέτρος δὲ is what the English carries.
ASV "asked to receive an alms" renders the infinitive λαβεῖν explicitly; the RP reading without it would give simply "asked alms".
ASV ends the command with "walk" alone; both longer readings prefix ἔγειρε/ἔγειραι ("rise up and walk"), which the ASV does not render.

English requires an object for "raised him up" whether or not the Greek prints αὐτόν after ἤγειρεν, and the first αὐτόν ("took him by the right hand") stands in both readings; the ASV wording does not distinguish them.
Word order only: αἱ βάσεις αὐτοῦ and αὐτοῦ αἱ βάσεις both yield ASV "his feet", and no note bears on the unit.
σφυδρά and σφυρά are orthographic variants of the same word; both are "his ankle-bones" in English.
Word order only: either order gives ASV "all the people saw him".
δὲ and τε are both connectives that ASV "and they took knowledge of him" renders identically.
ASV "that it was he that sat for alms" renders a resumptive pronoun that οὗτος and αὐτὸς both supply; the English does not mark the difference.

ASV "And as he held Peter and John" renders a bare pronoun; the RP reading τοῦ ἰαθέντος χωλοῦ would appear as "the lame man that was healed", which the ASV does not have. The verse note is alternative_rendering ("Or, portico") and bears on στοά, not this unit.
Article only: English needs "the porch" whether or not the Greek prints the article, so ASV wording cannot decide it.
Word order only: both orders give ASV "all the people ran together unto them".
Article with a proper name has no English reflex; ASV "when Peter saw it" is the same either way.
ASV "The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob" does not repeat "the God of"; the NA reading ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ would be rendered with the repetition, as ASV does at Mt. 22:32.
μὲν in ὃν ὑμεῖς μὲν παρεδώκατε is left untranslated in ASV "whom ye delivered up", so its presence or absence is invisible in the English.
ASV "and denied before the face of Pilate" carries no object for "denied"; the added αὐτὸν would give "denied him" (so KJV).

The dative τῇ πίστει alone renders as ASV "by faith" as readily as with ἐπὶ; the only note here is alternative_rendering ("Or, on the ground of"), which is about English wording and cannot decide the reading.
ASV "by the mouth of all the prophets" has no possessive; the RP addition αὐτοῦ would give "all his prophets".
ASV "that his Christ should suffer" renders the possessive αὐτοῦ, which the RP reading omits.
πρὸς τό and εἰς τό with the infinitive are both ASV "that your sins may be blotted out".
ASV "by the mouth of his holy prophets" has no "all"; the RP addition πάντων would be rendered.
Word order only: ASV renders ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος as the relative clause "that have been from of old", whose English position follows the noun on either Greek order.
ASV "Moses indeed said, A prophet shall the Lord God raise up" renders μὲν but has no addressee; the RP addition γὰρ πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας would give "for said unto the fathers".
ASV "the Lord God" carries no possessive; the Treg/NIV ὑμῶν would give "the Lord your God" and RP ἡμῶν "the Lord our God".
ἂν and ἐὰν are interchangeable here in the relative clause; ASV "that shall not hearken" is the same either way.
ASV "Ye are the sons of the prophets" renders the article of the predicate οἱ υἱοί; without οἱ the phrase would be "ye are sons of the prophets".
Word order only: both give ASV "the covenant which God made with your fathers".
ASV "with your fathers" renders ὑμῶν, not the RP ἡμῶν ("our fathers").
ἐνευλογηθήσονται and εὐλογηθήσονται are both ASV "shall ... be blessed"; the compound prefix has no separate English reflex.
Word order only: both give ASV "God, having raised up his Servant".

ASV "having raised up his Servant, sent him" has no name; the RP addition Ἰησοῦν would give "his Servant Jesus" (as ASV does render Ἰησοῦν at 3:13). The note is alternative_rendering on παῖς and does not touch this unit.
